Answer: C
Reason: The radiograph shows bilateral, asymmetric peribronchovascular consolidations and nodular opacities predominantly in the mid and lower lung zones, which is a classic presentation of pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma in an HIV-positive patient with known cutaneous disease. Unlike Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (which typically presents with symmetric perihilar ground-glass opacities) or bacterial pneumonia (usually lobar), these flame-shaped or nodular infiltrates tracking along bronchovascular bundles are highly characteristic of KS.
